identity.name: Thermally oxidized soya bean oil interacted with mono- and diglycerides of fatty acids
synonyms: Oxidised soya bean oil interacted with mono- and diglycerides of fatty acids
identity.chemical_class: Complex mixture of glycerol esters and fatty-acid-derived components from thermally oxidized soybean oil and mono-/diglycerides

function.mechanism: Amphiphilic glyceride/oxidized lipid ester mixture that helps stabilize fat-containing emulsions and modifies fat physical behavior in high-fat systems.
common_food_categories: Other fat and oil emulsions including spreads and liquid emulsions (EU FC 02.2.2)
Frying fat emulsions (restricted use context in EU authorization)

adi.basis: EFSA FAF (2018) stated available toxicological data were insufficient to support the current ADI; historical SCF/JECFA ADIs (25/30) were noted but not retained by EFSA as supported values.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA concluded use of E479b is of no safety concern at current limited uses (MoS about 540), but identified major data gaps (ADME, developmental toxicity, and no direct genotoxicity dataset).

fda.cfr_citation: No direct listing found in Title 21 CFR for E479b/TOSOM/CAS 884318-13-2 via eCFR search (accessed 2026-02-27). Related but non-identical substance: 21 CFR 172.818 (Oxystearin).
fda.notes: eCFR search for the additive name, synonyms, and CAS returned zero direct Title 21 hits; 21 CFR 172.818 allows oxystearin as crystallization inhibitor/release agent up to 0.125% in oils/shortenings.

adi.basis: WHO/JECFA database entry for TOSOM (Chemical 2334, INS 479) lists ADI as 0-30 mg/kg bw.

concerns.summary: EFSA reported no direct genotoxicity dataset for TOSOM; potential reactive manufacturing by-products (e.g., epoxides) were discussed as a theoretical concern.
Core toxicology package was incomplete (insufficient ADME data and no reliable developmental toxicity studies), limiting confidence in a formal ADI-based assessment.

no_concern_confirmed: 2.5-year rat chronic/carcinogenicity study (PubMed 8258411) did not show treatment-related carcinogenicity.
EFSA identified NOAEL 5,400 mg/kg bw/day (males; highest tested) and concluded no safety concern for current limited EU uses based on MoS.
Subchronic pig study cited by EFSA reported no adverse effects up to 4,000 mg/kg bw/day (limited study design).

adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA maximum-scenario exposure reached 10.1 mg/kg bw/day (P95) in toddlers, below historical SCF/JECFA ADIs; however EFSA considered available data insufficient to support retaining a formal ADI.

risk_assessment.rationale: Current authorized-use exposure appears low relative to observed NOAELs, but the toxicology package has material gaps (ADME/developmental/genotoxicity data limitations), so confidence is moderate rather than high.
key_factors: EFSA 2018: no safety concern at current limited use with MoS about 540
EFSA 2018: toxicological data insufficient to support current ADI
No IARC classification identified for this additive
No direct U.S. Title 21 listing identified for this specific substance
Direct PubMed literature on E479b/TOSOM is sparse and largely legacy
